- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or low (especially <0.2) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Forecast tends to lag true price drops — especially after sharp declines; model often holds too long.
- After a spike in price, model overcorrects downward, then undercorrects — creates “overshoot then undershoot” pattern.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices return to historical mean too quickly, ignoring sentiment-driven volatility.
- Sentiment decay matters: if sentiment drops below 0.2 over 3–5 days, model should reduce forecast slope.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early periods; adjust downward by 5–10% if sentiment is weak or trending down.
- Don’t ignore recent sentiment — if last 3–5 sentiment values are negative, reduce forecast by 3–7% to avoid overconfidence.
